title: Find the commit that broke it

terminal.description: A shell in your workspace. Run the setup to build the repository, then work inside repo/ with git.

tasks.title: Name the first bad commit
tasks.description:
Run `node setup.mjs`, then work inside `repo/`.

`node check.mjs` fails on `main` but passed at the commit `Add fare calculator and check`. Use `git bisect` (by hand or with `git bisect run`) to find the first commit where it fails.

Write that commit's hash in `repo/bisect-result.txt` (the full hash, or at least 7 characters). The check reads the first hash in the file and expects it to be exactly the first bad commit, not the last good one and not a later broken one.
nextSteps: Run `node setup.mjs`, `cd repo`, then `node check.mjs` to see the failure.
Find the hash of the commit that added the fare calculator with `git log --oneline`.
Start a bisect between main and that commit, and test each step.
Save the hash bisect reports into `bisect-result.txt`.
hints: You have a known good commit, a known bad one and a script that tells them apart. That is all bisect needs.
`check.mjs` exits 1 when a case fails, so `git bisect run` can run it at each step for you.
Start with main as bad and the fare calculator commit as good. The line ending in `is the first bad commit` has the hash to save.

tasks.title: Fix it in a new commit
tasks.description:
Fix the group discount in `fares.mjs` on `main`.

The check expects:

- `main` has at least one new commit on top of the original history, which is otherwise unchanged
- the original `node check.mjs` passes on `main`'s last commit
- bike tickets, added after the bug, still work: they cost 100 and do not count towards the group size
- the bisect is over, HEAD is on `main`, and the working tree is clean (`bisect-result.txt` is ignored by the repository)
nextSteps: End the bisect so you are back on main.
Compare the first bad commit with its parent to see what changed.
Fix `fares.mjs` on main and run `node check.mjs`.
Commit the fix without opening an editor.
hints: The guilty commit was a rewrite, and only one small detail of it changed the behavior.
Read the condition that decides whether the discount applies. Which group sizes does it include?
Groups of exactly four should get the discount. Change that comparison on main, keep the bike code, then `git commit -am` with a clear message.
